reviewer: independent read-only subagent (Explore type, fresh context), model opus

findings.finding: The README's headline numbers are out of date: bench/results/route-none.json and route-jev.json were written in c83ddf5, six minutes before 2b90d97 reworded 14 task prompts with '(it finds test/*.test.mjs; ...)'. FILE_RE now counts '.test.mjs' as a file, so 11 tasks reach files=3, the 'checked' rule (files<=2) no longer fires and they route to sonnet. Current ruleTier gives 5 haiku / 13 sonnet, the cached file 16 / 2. Re-scored, rules-only is 45% of opus cost, not 10-14%.
findings.resolution: accepted by the user for this run (2026-10-18), not fixed. Tool bug, not fixed. Confirmed independently by the orchestrator (current rules route 11/18 bench prompts to sonnet).

findings.finding: In 8 of 12 arm-B runs, arm B is the same setup as arm A (sonnet for r1-rename, f1-paginate, d3-maplimit, d5-deps, both repetitions). Only e1-locate and e2-count (Explore lookups) differ, so the success criterion is decided by two trivial lookup tasks; coding-task decisions are not tested. The 4 identical pairs measure run-to-run noise only.
findings.resolution: accepted by the user for this run (2026-10-18), not fixed. Property of what the router returns for these prompts, not a setup error; stated in the headline and deviations. A harder case set would be a new experiment.

findings.finding: The arms do not get the same number of attempts: B retries a failed check at the next tier, A keeps its failure.
findings.resolution: fixed in design.md (amendment): no escalation happened (24/24 first-attempt passes), so first-attempt and cascade pass rates are equal.

findings.finding: The leak check (subagent_usage --forbid) reads only tool inputs; a Grep/Glob over the repo would show hidden/ and solution/ in its OUTPUT without any forbidden word in the input.
findings.resolution: fixed: scan_results.mjs also scans tool results and inputs for bench/tasks, hidden/, solution/, check.mjs, mutants and the skill path: 0 hits in 24 agents (evidence/leak-scan.json). The answer keys still sit in the repo the agents could read.

findings.finding: Rules and benchmark were tuned on each other and no test pins them together: nothing runs ruleTier over the 18 bench prompts against route-*.json, so the drift in finding 1 passed 29/29 tests. 23 of 54 score cells are imputed and 12 of 18 tasks ran on Haiku only.
findings.resolution: accepted by the user for this run (2026-10-18), not fixed.

findings.finding: Self-consistency falls back to a single vote when provider calls fail: consistency() drops failed answers and calls one survivor 'stable'; with k=3, two timeouts and one 'haiku' gives haiku (a test asserts it).
findings.resolution: accepted by the user for this run (2026-10-18), not fixed.

findings.finding: Opus cacheRead price 0.2 USD/MTok is 0.05x its input price; Sonnet and Haiku use 0.1x. Every 'cost vs opus' ratio and this run's weighting use that table. Sonnet-vs-Haiku weights (what decides this run) are unaffected.
findings.resolution: not fixed; no Opus agent ran, so only the Sonnet/Haiku prices enter this run.

findings.finding: A baseline may be a strawman for the Explore cases: e1/e2 are routed as type Explore but run as general-purpose on sonnet in A; a real Explore subagent may already default to a cheaper model.
findings.resolution: not fixed; noted in deviations. The tool README pilot also ran everything as general-purpose.

findings.finding: Cost metric omits the orchestrator's own tokens and the routing calls (3 Jev calls and one Bash round-trip per B case), all of which favour B.
findings.resolution: not fixed; stated in design.md and deviations. Jev latency per route 0.7-1.5 s, about $0.00005 per call.

findings.finding: FILE_RE counts glob fragments and dotted names as files, so a parenthetical about how to run tests changes the tier; size and 'checked' rules depend on wording.
findings.resolution: not fixed (same root as the Critical drift finding).

findings.finding: Shadow mode with provider jev still sends k=3 OpenRouter calls with up to 6000 chars of every Agent prompt although nothing is applied; Jev labels are compared case-sensitively; route failure leaves model null and design.md did not say what B runs then.
findings.resolution: not fixed (route never failed in this run; all 12 B routes returned a tier).

findings.finding: Re-run `bench.mjs route` (none and jev) on the current prompts, re-score, correct the README ('18 tests' is now 29) and add a test that ruleTier for every bench prompt matches the cached file.
